newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean employers to sue union leaders.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean employers to sue union leaders.

text.p: South Korea's leading employers' groups on Monday agreed to sue union leaders for losses caused by strikes that the government has declared illegal, a spokesman for the employers said.

"We will sue those who have led illegal actions at production sites," Byun Hae-ryong, a director of the Korea Employers' Federation, told reporters after a meeting of representatives from five leading employers' groups and top 15 conglomerates.
He gave no details of exactly who would be sued, and when legal action would be taken.
Byun said strikes cost employers 340 billion won ($403 million) in lost production between December 26 and January 3.
Earlier on Monday, state prosecutors summoned about 20 leaders of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions over protests and strikes called since December 26.
